summary: Idiofa territory part 1 (Kwilu) covers Idiofa town and the Idiofa and Ipamu secteurs, including the Kasai river towns of Mangai and Dibaya-Lubwe. No armed group is reported to control or regularly raid any locality here: Radio Okapi coverage of Idiofa, Mangai and Dibaya-Lubwe in 2025-2026 concerns unpaid teachers, electricity, weather and ordinary crime, not militia activity, and the Mobondo militia remains confined to the Maï-Ndombe border areas of Kwilu (Bagata, Bulungu) far to the west, where the government reported it in retreat in March 2026. All locations are assessed as under ordinary state authority, with the PNC and the parquet/courts of Idiofa as the main coercive and justice institutions and customary chiefs under them. Confidence is medium for the main towns and low for villages, as evidence is the absence of reported armed-group activity rather than positive reporting on police posts.

zones.description: Idiofa town, territorial seat (Idiofa health zone, Kizito health areas)
zones.evidence: Territorial seat with territorial administration, PNC commissariat, courts and prison; no armed group reported controlling or regularly raiding the town. No source reports armed-group activity in this area as of the reference date; the Mobondo militia theatre (Kwamouth, Bagata, Kenge, Kwango) lies far to the west. Review (2026-10-01): Radio Okapi/AllAfrica coverage of Idiofa territory in 2025-2026 (teacher salary strikes, Kakobola power supply, a death in Mangai forest, ordinary criminality) reports no armed group; Mobondo activity in Kwilu is limited to the Maï-Ndombe border zones and was described as in retreat in March 2026.
